prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;covers Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport;local/statutory authority retained. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove. Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message(route/timing/registration/turnaround/crew/connections);Identity Access Service authenticates;Business Rules Registry maps carriers;invalid/incomplete rejected with machine-readable reasons;material intents supersede schedules,changes require messages. Marlinstone updates demand;Capacity Assessment Module compares Airport Capacity Plan/Airport Acceptance Rate;Storm Cell Snapshot qualifies confidence. Slot Allocation Engine→Adapter/Portal:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time. Ground Delay Program:Slot Coordinator checks equity/feasibility,logs accepted/rejected adjustments/unresolved conflicts;Copperfin authorizes baseline/recovery/divergence. Saffron maintains intents/readiness/constraints,checks legality/rotations/maintenance/passengers. Orchard validates identity/time/location/units;retain probability/provenance/version/override;degradation visible,low-confidence capacity provisional. Meteorology Briefing Officer attaches interpretation/confidence/impact-timing without replacing authoritative source;may override. Time Synchronization Service timestamps transactions→Audit Event Ledger. Alert Distribution Hub→Copperfin/Tower Supervisor/Saffron/accountable updater. Capacities→North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter;East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Ramp Movement Board:weather/taxi correlation. Ramp Control Lead maintains stand-release/conflicts/tugs/pushback. Tower Supervisor validates runway assumptions/departure feasibility/tactical constraints via Tower Sequence Manager. Airport Duty Manager maintains capacity/impacts,checks terminal/passengers via Common Situation Display,confirms Normal Operations/Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State/Recovery Phase. Ground Handling Dispatcher updates servicing/baggage/staffing/equipment immediately. Portal role-restricts workspaces;publishes synchronized demand/constraints automatically each cycle;tracks stands/aircraft/decisions/departure-arrival milestones(planned/target/estimated/actual/manual). Display distinguishes service/user-confirmed/stale values;Portal highlights stale flights,alerts accountable roles. Material changes:≤2 minutes Normal,≤1 minute

New part:
S173: After operations, the Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded milestones and decision history to compare planned outcomes with actual off-block, takeoff, landing, and stand events.
S174: Tower and airport duty coordination establishes the working link between live control positions, the airport duty desk, surface surveillance feeds, and operational safety checks.
S175: The Tower Supervisor remains accountable for control tower coordination and keeps the Airport Duty Manager informed of conditions that may affect runway, taxiway, stand, or apron availability.
S176: For this section only, Brindle is the operational alias used by Tower Supervisor during voice coordination drills.
S177: The Airport Duty Manager maintains the airport duty desk as the single operational point for airport status confirmation during Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase.
S178: The duty desk reviews tower inputs, airport operations reports, and surveillance indications before confirming whether a local condition should be reflected in the Airport Capacity Plan.
S179: The Surface Surveillance Adapter consolidates position updates from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor and presents movement indications to the Airport CDM Portal.
S180: The Tower Sequence Manager uses validated surface status to support local sequencing decisions without replacing controller judgment or established radio procedures.
S181: The Airport Duty Manager uses the Runway Inspection Note to confirm that the duty desk has a current record of pavement status before endorsing any declared capacity change.
S182: Orchard shall issue time-stamped weather condition updates for use in tower and airport duty coordination.
S183: When surveillance data conflicts with tower observations, the Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager agree on the operational interpretation before the condition is shared more widely.
S184: The Ramp Control Lead reviews apron movement constraints with the duty desk when stand access, pushback flow, or tug routing affects the departure plan.
S185: The Airport CDM Portal records duty desk confirmations as operational annotations linked to the relevant runway, taxiway, apron, or stand area.
S186: The Collaborative Decision Log captures the time, origin, and rationale for each local coordination decision that affects capacity or surface flow.
S187: The Time Synchronization Service shall keep tower, duty desk, surveillance, and portal event times aligned so that later review can reconstruct the sequence of events.
S188: Surface surveillance feeds are treated as advisory evidence for airport duty decisions unless the competent controller or airport authority confirms the operational effect.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
